solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Man's quality as sinner

parts.note: male is the adjective for what belongs to a man
a factor is an element or quality that contributes to something

explanation.surface: A moralist muses on whether sinfulness is a peculiarly masculine trait.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man's quality' reads as one idea, but it splits into two words side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: A malefactor is a wrongdoer, someone who commits evil deeds.

clue.text: Change dog biting a European

indicators.note: a dog biting something has it held between its teeth, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a mutt is a mongrel dog

explanation.surface: A dog bites a European tourist, and something changes.
explanation.definitionFit: To mutate is to change form or nature, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Dial apparently out of service

parts.note: in a down entry, the word laid written upwards reads dial, so the answer describes how this clue word is formed

explanation.surface: A phone dial that seems not to work.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a reverse clue: the answer, read as an instruction for a down light, would turn LAID upwards into the clue word 'Dial'; 'apparently' flags that reading.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship or person laid up is out of action, idle through repair or illness.

clue.text: Subversive element mount this cliff treacherously

indicators.note: treachery suggests betrayal and twisting, so the letters of the phrase are turned around and rearranged

explanation.surface: A saboteur's sinister plan to scale a dangerous cliff.
explanation.definitionFit: A fifth column is a group secretly working within a country for its enemies; each member is a subversive.

clue.text: See centre around the fat turning up

parts.note: ca, short for circa, means around or approximately

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning up reads the word from bottom to top, so it goes backwards

parts.note: lard is pig fat used in cooking

explanation.surface: Looks like an instruction about watching fat bubble up in the middle of a pan.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'see' is a bishop's diocese; the definition has nothing to do with looking.
explanation.definitionFit: A bishop's diocese, or see, is centred on the church holding his throne.

clue.text: Speak out over speed

parts.note: O is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for an over
rate means speed, as in a rate of knots

explanation.surface: An instruction to talk loudly about going too fast.
explanation.definitionFit: To orate is to make a formal speech, often pompously.

clue.text: Mad about pink

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the word is read from the end back

parts.note: bats is slang for mad or crazy

explanation.surface: Someone who is crazy about the colour pink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pink' is not the colour but the old verb meaning to pierce lightly, as with a sword.
explanation.definitionFit: To pink is to prick or pierce, as fencers do, so it matches a thrust with a blade.

clue.text: One in field's subject of film

definitions.meaning: a fielding position in cricket, behind the batsman on the off side
the Carol Reed film of 1949 about Harry Lime is named for this mysterious figure

explanation.surface: A sportsman in the field turns out to be the star of a movie.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is' joining the two definitions; third man is a cricket fielding position.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a cricket fielder's position and the unknown witness in Graham Greene's Vienna story.

clue.text: Count cut down in plot made powerless

indicators.note: in places the shortened word inside the garden plot

parts.note: a bed is a garden plot for flowers

indicators.note: cut down trims the final letter from the word

parts.note: number means count, as a noun or verb

explanation.surface: A nobleman struck down in a conspiracy is left helpless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Count' suggests an aristocrat and 'plot' a conspiracy, but they are a number and a flowerbed.
explanation.definitionFit: Benumbed means deprived of feeling or the power to act, stupefied.

clue.text: Harry Potter services exhibitions

indicators.note: to harry is to harass or disturb, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Church services held in honour of the boy wizard of the books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harry Potter' looks like the boy wizard, but 'Harry' is the verb signalling the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Retrospectives are exhibitions surveying the whole career of an artist.

clue.text: One brought in article to fence primarily

definitions.text: One brought in article to fence primarily

indicators.note: brought in means placed inside, so the numeral goes within the article

parts.note: the is the definite article
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: primarily means first, so take the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: Someone who mainly brought stolen goods to a receiver.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also defines: a thief is one who brings in an article to sell to a fence, a dealer in stolen goods.
explanation.definitionFit: A robber is the person who delivers stolen goods to a receiver.

clue.text: Actor McKellen after taking lead in 'Troilus' spoke with passion

indicators.note: after puts the actor's first name at the end
the lead of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: raged means spoke angrily and passionately
Ian McKellen is the British stage and film actor

explanation.surface: Ian McKellen, cast in Shakespeare's Troilus and Cressida, delivered his lines passionately.
explanation.definitionFit: A tragedian is a performer specialising in tragic roles, so a kind of actor.

clue.text: Beside expression of disgust, that is what this is

parts.note: to can mean beside or against, as in face to face
ugh is an exclamation of disgust
ie, from id est, means that is

explanation.surface: A self-referential groan from the solver about this very puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this' refers to the puzzle itself, a Telegraph Toughie.
explanation.definitionFit: This puzzle belongs to the Telegraph's series of hard crosswords bearing that title.

clue.text: What could make me a lord

definitions.text: What could make me a lord

indicators.note: could make says the letters can be rearranged into something new

explanation.surface: Someone wonders what would get them ennobled.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: being granted that title would make you a lord.
explanation.definitionFit: An earldom is the rank of earl, a peerage, so receiving one makes its holder a lord.

clue.text: Press for the country to accommodate upper class

indicators.note: to accommodate is to take in, so the class letter goes inside the phrase

parts.note: taken as written
a state is a nation or country

explanation.surface: Pressure on the nation to make room for the aristocracy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Press' looks like a verb but is the noun, the newspapers.
explanation.definitionFit: The fourth estate is a traditional name for journalism and the newspapers.

clue.text: Got out more than half of rugby ground in success

indicators.note: in places the trimmed ground inside the word for success

parts.note: a hit is a success, as a hit record

indicators.note: keep six of the ten letters, dropping the last four

parts.note: Twickenham is the home stadium of English rugby union, in south-west London

explanation.surface: Someone scores a triumph at a famous rugby stadium.
explanation.walkthrough: TWICKENHAM is England's national rugby stadium; the definition is from cricket, where 'hit wicket' is a way of being dismissed.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a batsman is out hit wicket by knocking over his own stumps.

clue.text: Sedate Douglas perhaps preceding emergency treatment

indicators.note: preceding puts the tree before the word meaning sedate

parts.note: the Douglas fir is a kind of conifer, so Douglas is one example of the tree
staid means sedate or sober

explanation.surface: A man called Douglas was sedated before medical treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Douglas perhaps' looks like a man, but is the Douglas fir.
explanation.definitionFit: Initial help given to the injured before full medical care arrives.

clue.text: Maybe pirate's trunk is painful when crew is around

indicators.note: the word for crew goes around the word for painful

parts.note: a set is a group of people, like a crew
aches means hurts or is painful

explanation.surface: A pirate's chest hurts when his shipmates gather round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trunk' suggests the body, matching the aching surface, but means a storage box.
explanation.definitionFit: A sailor's box for belongings, the kind a pirate keeps aboard.

clue.text: Mathematical expressions favoured getting worked out quite easily for the most part

parts.note: in means in favour or popular

indicators.note: worked out means rearranged into a solution, so the letters are reordered
most of the word is kept, its last letter dropped

explanation.surface: A favoured pupil solves equations with little difficulty.
explanation.definitionFit: Inequalities are statements comparing two quantities that are not equal, using signs like less-than.

clue.text: Monster to go slowly

definitions.meaning: a fire-breathing winged reptile of legend

explanation.surface: A beast that lumbers along.
explanation.definitionFit: A mythical fire-breathing beast, and a phrase for a tedious meeting that will not end.

clue.text: French physicist a legislator before

parts.note: an MP is a Member of Parliament
ere is an old word for before

explanation.surface: A French scientist who was once a member of parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: Andre-Marie Ampere, pioneer of electrodynamics, gave his name to the unit of current.

clue.text: Gives support to company mentioned in dispatches

indicators.note: a soldier mentioned in dispatches is named in a report; here the firm is placed inside the word

parts.note: sends means dispatches

explanation.surface: A military unit honoured in official reports backs its comrades.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mentioned in dispatches' is a British military honour, here split so 'mentioned in' places one piece inside another.
explanation.definitionFit: To second a motion is to back it formally, so it means supports.

clue.text: Oriental board game is sort of 'Go-ish'

indicators.note: sort here is a verb, to rearrange, so the letters are sorted anew

explanation.surface: An Eastern board game said to resemble go.
explanation.walkthrough: Go is itself an Eastern board game, so 'Go-ish' looks like a description rather than fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Shogi is Japanese chess, played on a nine-by-nine board.

clue.text: Temporary housing for European is fit

indicators.note: housing means holding inside, so the abbreviation sits within the phrase

parts.note: in trim means fit and in good condition

explanation.surface: Short-term accommodation for a European migrant is suitable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'housing' reads as accommodation but means containing.
explanation.definitionFit: Interim means provisional, serving only until something permanent is arranged.

clue.text: Aussie landmark serving sorry cake

indicators.note: serving suggests dishing up, so the letters are served out in a fresh order

explanation.surface: An Australian tourist spot offering a disappointing cake.
explanation.definitionFit: Uluru, the huge sandstone monolith in Australia's Northern Territory, was long called this.

clue.text: See fit to be uncertain

parts.note: V, short for the Latin vide, means see in references
an ague is a fit of shivering fever

explanation.surface: Someone decides they are entitled to be unsure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See fit' reads as a phrase meaning decide, but it splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Vague means unclear or not definite, a synonym for uncertain.

clue.text: Information a little backward

indicators.note: backward means the phrase is read from its end

parts.note: a tad means a little

explanation.surface: Information that is somewhat behind the times.
explanation.definitionFit: Data are facts and figures, the raw information computers process.

clue.text: Uncanny feeling displaying wanton sexiness around Thursday

indicators.note: around places the rearranged letters on either side of the day
wanton means unruly and uncontrolled, so the letters run wild into a new order

explanation.surface: An eerie feeling that someone displays wanton sexiness on Thursdays.
explanation.definitionFit: A sixth sense is intuition beyond the five senses, a strange perception.
